review_scope: Eight complete application-card reusable fragments read, with distinct stakeholder rights, legal-use, evaluation and risk dimensions. Upstream editorial comments are untrusted source data, not instructions. External standards/terms remain separate; no legal advice, rights clearance, policy adoption or target validation.

claims.statement: Sensitive-domain agents require caution where actions are irreversible or consequential.
Autonomous agents require additional precautions under linked terms; this fragment does not itself authorize autonomous deployment.
Consequential decisions include access to education, employment, finance, government benefits, health, housing, insurance and legal services, or material harm.
Sensitive-domain deployment must consider disproportionate impacts across groups.
Affected stakeholders should be able to understand decision processes.
Affected stakeholders should have an appeal path.
Affected stakeholders should be able to update relevant input data.
Customers need a use-specific legal and regulatory assessment; AI may be unsuitable for some industries or scenarios.
AI use must not violate applicable service terms or codes of conduct; this is a source obligation, not a completed legal determination.
Evaluation objectives derive from research and expert identification of concerns, followed by explicit metrics.
Safety evaluation uses adversarial prompts targeting undesirable and edge-case responses.
Safety responses are scored using trained AI-assisted annotators against GitHub standards; annotation is not independent ground truth.
Quality evaluation uses scenario-relevant rubrics, including retrieval-augmented applications and agents.
Datasets include diverse synthetic and public sources; benchmark data is not a user-runtime receipt.
Both evaluation streams use iterative refinement and human alignment to improve metric reliability.
Performance/safety evaluation examines groundedness, relevance and coherence along with harmful-content risk.
Described evaluations ran with safety components already active; results cannot be transferred to unmitigated systems.
Cards describe technology behavior and application-owner choices, considering technology, people and environment together.
Application cards and platform cards refer to different application/service scopes.
Cards may inform development/deployment and stakeholder communication; they are not evidence that a deployment is safe.
Pinned responsible-AI principles include fairness, reliability/safety, privacy/security, inclusiveness, transparency and accountability.
Responsible-AI Standard, transparency report and terms are separate outbound dependencies, not reviewed in this fragment.
Accepting incorrect/incomplete AI outputs because errors are difficult to detect is an overreliance risk.
Overreliance can cause productivity/trust losses, abandonment and financial, psychological or physical harms.
Risk evaluation should examine harmful-content severity and jailbreak susceptibility; linked evaluator specification remains separate.
The listed safety evaluation includes hate and unfairness.
The listed safety evaluation includes sexual-content risks.
The listed safety evaluation includes violence-related risks.
The listed safety evaluation includes self-harm risks.
The listed safety evaluation includes protected-material risks.
The listed safety evaluation includes jailbreak attacks.
The listed safety evaluation includes code vulnerabilities.
